mainTopic: Guarding animals properly: the opening משנה of פרק הכונס צאן, whose view it follows, the Torah's lighter guarding for שן and רגל, and four cases that are פטור in a human court but חייב בדיני שמים.
overview: This עמוד opens פרק הכונס צאן. Its משנה teaches that an owner who locked his sheep in the pen properly is פטור if they get out and do damage. If he locked it carelessly, left the animal in the sun, or handed it to a חרש, שוטה, or קטן, he is חייב. If לסטים took the sheep out, they pay, and if he handed the animal to a רועה, the רועה takes his place. The משנה also covers an animal that fell into a garden or walked in, and רבי שמעון's rule for ripe produce. The גמרא defines proper locking as a door that holds against a normal wind. It then asks whose view the משנה follows: רבי יהודה, who allows weaker guarding for a מועד, or even רבי מאיר, because the Torah lowered the guarding needed for שן and רגל, as it did for בור and אש. רבה tries to prove the רבי מאיר reading from the word צאן, but the גמרא shows the word fits רבי יהודה too. Finally, a ברייתא of רבי יהושע lists four cases that are פטור in a human court but חייב בדיני שמים. The גמרא begins explaining the first case, breaking a fence, and that explanation continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Locking the pen properly or not properly
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens the chapter. An owner who locked his sheep in the pen properly is פטור if they get out and damage. An owner who did not lock it properly is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone brought his sheep into the pen. If he locked the door the right way and they still got out and did damage, he does not pay. If he did not lock it the right way and they got out and did damage, he pays.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its first and basic rule. Whether the owner pays depends on whether he locked the pen the right way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The damage is exactly the same in both cases. The only difference is how well the owner guarded the sheep. This teaches that liability here is tied to proper guarding: once the owner has done what he should, he is פטור even if damage happens anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the abbreviation מַתְנִי׳ marks the start of the משנה)
Pen or enclosure for sheep
He locked
As is proper; the right way
Exempt; does not have to pay
Liable; has to pay

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the anchor of the whole chapter. Every later case in the משנה is measured against the question of whether the owner guarded properly.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who brings sheep into the pen,
and locked the door before it properly,
phrases.notes: The word 'it' means the flock of sheep.

phrases.english: and it went out and caused damage – he is exempt.
If he did not lock the door before it properly,
and it went out and caused damage – he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the משנה and the new chapter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Locked properly: פטור. Not locked properly: חייב.

steps.title: The wall breaks or bandits break in
steps.stepSummary: The pen was locked properly, but the wall broke at night or לסטים broke it. If the sheep then got out and damaged, the owner is פטור. If the לסטים took the sheep out themselves, the לסטים are חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the pen's wall broke open at night, or robbers broke it open, and the sheep got out and did damage, the owner does not pay. If the robbers themselves took the sheep out, the robbers pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds cases where something outside the owner's control opened the pen. It also shows when the responsibility moves to the robbers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wall breaks by itself or robbers break it, the owner did nothing wrong, so he is פטור. But when the לסטים actually took the animals out, they took control of them. So they are the ones who are חייב for the damage.

keyTerms.meaning: It was breached; broke open
Bandits; robbers
They took it out

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two robber cases. If the לסטים only broke the wall and the sheep wandered out on their own, nobody in the משנה is said to pay. Only when the לסטים themselves took the sheep out are they חייב.

phrases.english: If it was breached at night
or bandits breached it,
and it went out and caused damage – he is exempt.
If bandits took it out – the bandits are liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the 'locked properly' case and adds outside forces that open the pen.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wall broke or לסטים broke it: owner פטור. לסטים took the sheep out: לסטים חייב.

steps.title: Leaving the animal in the sun or with someone who cannot guard it
steps.stepSummary: If the owner left the animal in the sun, or gave it to a חרש, שוטה, or קטן, and it got out and damaged, the owner is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he left the animal in the sun, or gave it over to a deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, or a child, and it got out and did damage, the owner pays.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now lists two kinds of owner carelessness that make him חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In these cases the owner did not really guard the animal. Putting it in the sun hurts it. Handing it to a חרש, שוטה, or קטן is handing it to someone who cannot guard it. So it is as if the owner left it unguarded, and he pays.

keyTerms.meaning: The sun; the heat of the sun
A deaf-mute
A mentally incompetent person
A minor; a child

phrases.english: If he left it in the sun,
or he gave it over to a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor,
and it went out and caused damage – he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the cases where the owner is פטור, the משנה gives cases of careless guarding where he is חייב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Left in the sun, or given to a חרש, שוטה, or קטן: the owner is חייב.

steps.title: Handing the animal to a shepherd
steps.stepSummary: If the owner gave the animal to a רועה, the רועה takes the owner's place and is the one responsible.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he gave the animal to a shepherd, the shepherd steps into the owner's place.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list of guarding cases with one where the responsibility for guarding moves to someone else, the רועה. The משנה then goes on to an animal that got into a garden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the opposite of handing the animal to a חרש, שוטה, or קטן. A רועה is able to guard, so the duty to guard passes to him. He now stands where the owner stood.

keyTerms.meaning: He handed it over
Shepherd
Enters in his place; takes over his role

steps.whatToRemember: The whole משנה follows one idea: whoever is supposed to be guarding the animal and failed to guard it properly is the one who pays. If the owner guarded properly, he is פטור. If he was careless, he is חייב. If the לסטים took the sheep out, they pay. If a רועה took over the guarding, he takes the owner's place.

phrases.english: If he gave it over to a shepherd –
the shepherd enters in his place.
phrases.notes: 'His place' means the owner's place: the shepherd now carries the owner's responsibility.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with handing the animal to a חרש, שוטה, or קטן. Here the person receiving it can guard it, so the responsibility moves to him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A רועה who receives the animal takes over the owner's responsibility.

steps.title: Fell in versus walked in, and how damage is measured
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues. An animal that fell into a garden pays only for its benefit. An animal that walked in normally pays the full damage, measured by checking a בית סאה of that field.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the animal fell into a garden and enjoyed the food, the owner pays for what it enjoyed. If it walked down in its normal way and did damage, the owner pays for the damage. How is that damage paid? The court looks at a בית סאה of that field. It checks how much that area was worth before the damage and how much it is worth now.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two different payments: one for an animal that fell in, and one for an animal that walked in normally. Then it explains how the court measures the damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Falling in is an accident, so the owner pays only for the food the animal actually benefited from. Walking in normally is ordinary שן ורגל damage, so the owner pays the full loss. The loss is measured as part of a larger area, a בית סאה, not just the small spot that was eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: Benefits; the animal enjoyed the food.
In its normal way.
The court estimates the value.
An area of land large enough to plant one סאה of seed.

steps.confusionAlert: The court does not measure only the small patch that was eaten. It measures the drop in value of a whole בית סאה around it, so the payment comes out smaller.

phrases.english: If it fell into a garden and benefited —
it pays what it benefited.
If it went down in its normal way and damaged —
it pays what it damaged.
How does it pay what it damaged?
We estimate a בית סאה in that field —
how much it was worth,
and how much it is worth now.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with new cases of an animal that got into a garden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fell in: the owner pays the benefit. Walked in normally: the owner pays the damage, measured within a בית סאה.

steps.title: Ripe produce is paid in full
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says that if the animal ate fully ripe produce, the owner pays for exactly that amount of produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: if it ate fully ripe produce, the owner pays for fully ripe produce. If it ate one סאה, he pays one סאה. If it ate two סאה, he pays two סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון adds a limit to the way of measuring damage that the משנה just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ripe produce is already ready to sell, so measuring it as part of a larger field would not be fair. Instead, the owner pays for the exact amount that was eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: Fully ripe produce, ready to harvest.
Two סאה (a measure of volume).

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends here. Damage in a field is measured as part of a בית סאה, but according to רבי שמעון, ripe produce is paid in full, one for one.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
If it ate fully ripe produce —
it pays fully ripe produce.
If a סאה, a סאה;
if two סאה, two סאה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אָכְלָה פֵּירוֹת גְּמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the בית סאה way of measuring from step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ripe produce that was eaten is paid back in full, amount for amount.

steps.title: What counts as locking properly
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines 'properly': a door that can stand up to a normal wind is proper locking, and a door that cannot is not proper.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: What is 'properly' and what is 'not properly'? A door that can stand up to a normal wind is 'properly.' A door that cannot stand up to a normal wind is 'not properly.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by explaining the word כראוי ('properly') from the start of the משנה, where the owner locked the pen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה made the owner פטור if he locked the pen 'properly' (step 1). This ברייתא gives the measure: the door only needs to hold against an ordinary wind, not an unusual storm.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows the משנה.
Properly, as it should be.
An ordinary, normal wind.

phrases.english: Gemara: The Rabbis taught:
What is 'properly,'
and what is 'not properly'?
A door that can stand up to a normal wind —
this is 'properly.'
One that cannot stand up to a normal wind —
this is 'not properly.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the first line of the משנה (step 1) to define the word כראוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proper locking means a door that can withstand a normal wind.

steps.title: Which תנא allows weak guarding for a מועד
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני בר פטיש asks which תנא holds that a מועד animal needs only weaker guarding, and answers that it is רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מני בר פטיש said: Who is the תנא who holds that for a מועד, weaker guarding is enough? It is רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מני בר פטיש identifies the author of our משנה. He then sets up a proof from another משנה, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals eating and trampling (שן ורגל) are always treated as מועד. Our משנה still lets the owner off with a door that only holds against a normal wind, which is weaker guarding. So the משנה must follow a תנא who says a מועד needs only weaker guarding, and he says that is רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא, meaning which Sage's view is this?
An animal known to cause this type of damage.
Weaker, lesser guarding.
It is enough for it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Mani bar Patish said:
Who is the תנא who holds that a מועד
is fine with weaker guarding?
phrases.notes: He means our משנה, which accepted a door that only holds against a normal wind.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yehuda,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תַּנָּא מוּעָד דְּסַגִּי לֵיהּ בִּשְׁמִירָה פְּחוּתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the definition in step 7: such a door is weak guarding, so the גמרא asks whose view the משנה follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Our משנה follows רבי יהודה, who holds that a מועד needs only weaker guarding.
steps.whyThisMatters: It tells us that our משנה's ruling does not follow everyone. It depends on one side of a debate.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה: רבי מאיר's view
steps.stepSummary: The proof begins by quoting a משנה. רבי מאיר says that even with reins or a proper lock, the owner is חייב whether the ox is a תם or a מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If the owner tied it with reins, or locked the door in front of it properly, and it got out and did damage, the owner is חייב, whether it is a תם or a מועד. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting the משנה that proves the point. This step gives only רבי מאיר's view and sets up רבי יהודה's view, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, simple guarding like reins or a proper lock is not enough even for a מועד, so the owner is still חייב. That is the opposite of our משנה. So the משנה must follow the other opinion, רבי יהודה, which is quoted next.

keyTerms.meaning: Reins or a rope used to tie an animal.
An animal not known to cause this damage.

phrases.english: as we learned in a משנה:
If its owner tied it with reins,
or locked the door in front of it properly,
and it got out and did damage —
whether a תם or a מועד, he is חייב;
phrases.notes: This is about an ox that gores, from the משנה on דף מה.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the proof for step 8's claim that the משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that our משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה on דף מה: רבי מאיר holds that a proper lock is not enough even for a מועד, which points to רבי יהודה as the other view.

steps.title: רבי יהודה and רבי אליעזר finish the proof
steps.stepSummary: The משנה being quoted continues. רבי יהודה says a תם is חייב but a מועד that was guarded with a weaker guarding is פטור. רבי אליעזר says the only real guarding for a מועד is slaughtering it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: if the ox is a תם, the owner is liable. If it is a מועד, he is exempt, because the Torah says 'and its owner did not guard it,' and this one was guarded. רבי אליעזר says: the only guarding that works for it is a knife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה it started in Step 9. This shows that רבי יהודה is the one who says a weaker guarding is enough for a מועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds the owner is חייב either way, and רבי אליעזר says only slaughter counts. That leaves רבי יהודה as the only one who says weaker guarding exempts a מועד. This is exactly what רבי מני בר פטיש claimed.

keyTerms.meaning: An ox that has not yet built a record of goring. Its owner pays half damages.
An ox that has been 'warned,' meaning it has a record of goring. Its owner pays full damages.
Guarding: the steps an owner takes to keep his animal from causing damage.
A knife. Here it means slaughtering the animal.

steps.whatToRemember: Only רבי יהודה says that a weaker guarding (reins or a proper lock) is enough to exempt the owner of a מועד.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
An innocuous ox – he is liable; a forewarned ox – he is exempt;
phrases.notes: He means: when the owner tied it with reins or locked it in properly.

phrases.english: as it is said: "and its owner has not guarded it"
and this one was guarded.
Rabbi Eliezer says:
It has no guarding except a knife.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: תָּם – חַיָּיב, מוּעָד – פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה quotation begun in Step 9, finishing the proof for רבי מני בר פטיש.
steps.raayaObject: That our משנה (weaker guarding is enough) follows רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה listing the views of רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, and רבי אליעזר on guarding a מועד ox.

steps.title: Even רבי מאיר could agree, because eating and trampling are different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Our משנה could follow רבי מאיר too, because for שן ורגל the Torah itself lowered the guarding requirement.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say our משנה follows רבי מאיר. Eating and trampling are different, because the Torah lowered the guarding needed for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It says our משנה does not have to follow only רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's strict view was about goring (קרן). Our משנה is about an animal eating or trampling in a garden (שן ורגל). For those, the Torah itself made the guarding lighter, so even רבי מאיר would agree that weaker guarding is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You can even say': the גמרא shows that another view could also fit.
'It is different': this points out how one case is not like another.
Tooth and foot: damage an animal does by eating or trampling.
Lowered or reduced. Here it means the Torah made the guarding requirement lighter.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the cases. רבי מאיר's strict ruling was about a goring ox (קרן). The משנה here is about eating and trampling, which have their own lighter rule.

phrases.english: You can even say it is Rabbi Meir,
eating and trampling are different –
since the Torah lowered the guarding required for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from Steps 9-10 that our משנה must follow רבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the conclusion that our משנה must be רבי יהודה. It does not deny that רבי יהודה holds this view.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof compared goring (קרן) with eating and trampling (שן ורגל). But the Torah has a special lighter guarding rule for שן ורגל.

steps.title: Four damagers with lighter guarding
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר, or some say a ברייתא, teaches that the Torah lowered the guarding for four damagers: בור, אש, שן, and רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אלעזר said, and some say it was taught in a ברייתא: there are four things where the Torah lowered the guarding needed. They are: pit, fire, eating, and trampling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to back up its claim that שן ורגל have lighter guarding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list puts שן ורגל together with בור and אש as damagers whose guarding the Torah made lighter. This supports the claim in Step 11 that even רבי מאיר would accept weaker guarding for them.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא: a teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה.
Pit: damage caused by a hole someone dug or opened.
Fire: damage caused by a fire that spreads.

steps.whyThisMatters: This list is the basis for the rule that, for these four damagers, normal reasonable guarding exempts the owner.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Elazar said,
and some say it was taught in a ברייתא:
four things
the Torah lowered the guarding required for them,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן: בּוֹר, וָאֵשׁ, שֵׁן, וָרֶגֶל.
phrases.english: and these are they: pit, fire, eating, and trampling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim in Step 11 that the Torah lowered the guarding for שן ורגל.
steps.raayaObject: That the Torah lowered the guarding required for שן ורגל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of רבי אלעזר (or a ברייתא) listing four damagers with lighter guarding.

steps.title: The source for pit: covering it is enough
steps.stepSummary: From the פסוק 'and he did not cover it,' we learn that if he did cover the pit, he is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Pit: as it is written, 'If a man opens a pit, or if a man digs a pit, and does not cover it.' That means if he covered it, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts showing where the Torah lowers the guarding for each damager on the list, beginning with בור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק makes the owner pay only when he did not cover the pit. So simply covering it is enough guarding to exempt him, even though the cover could come off later.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As it is written': this introduces a פסוק.
He will cover it.
'But then': this introduces a conclusion learned from what the words imply.

phrases.english: Pit – as it is written:
"If a man opens a pit
or if a man digs a pit,
and does not cover it",
but if he covered it – he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins giving the פסוק for each item on the list from Step 12, starting with בור.
steps.raayaObject: That the Torah lowered the guarding required for a pit.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 21:33, 'and he does not cover it.'

steps.title: The source for fire: only when he acts like one who kindles
steps.stepSummary: From the פסוק 'the one who kindled the fire shall surely pay,' we learn that a person is חייב only when his carelessness is like actually lighting the fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fire: as it is written, 'The one who kindled the fire shall surely pay.' That means he is not liable unless he did something like kindling the fire himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the list and gives the source for אש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah calls the one who pays 'the one who kindled.' So he is חייב only if his carelessness is like starting the fire himself. If he guarded it reasonably, he is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who kindled: the person who started the fire.
The fire, or the burning.
Similar to, like.

phrases.english: Fire – as it is written:
"shall surely pay
the one who kindled the fire" –
not unless he acts like one who kindles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list from Step 12, after בור in Step 13, with the source for אש.
steps.raayaObject: That the Torah lowered the guarding required for fire.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 22:5, 'the one who kindled the fire shall surely pay.'

steps.title: The source for שן: 'and it feeds in another's field'
steps.stepSummary: For שן, the פסוק says 'וּבִעֵר', so the owner is חייב only when he acted like he let his animal graze there.
steps.simpleTranslation: For tooth, it is written: 'and it feeds in another's field.' This means he is not חייב until he acts in a way that is like 'and it feeds.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the third of the four damagers from step 12. It shows from the פסוק that the Torah lowered the guarding needed for שן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וּבִעֵר' describes the owner almost feeding his animal in someone else's field. So the owner is חייב only when his carelessness is that bad. A basic level of guarding is enough to make him פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: Tooth: damage an animal does by eating
'And it feeds' or 'and it consumes' (שמות 22:4)
Similar to, like

phrases.english: Tooth – as it is written:
phrases.notes: The גמרא means: where do we see the Torah lowered the guarding for tooth?

phrases.english: "and it feeds in another's field"
– he is not liable until he does something like "and it feeds."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list from step 12 after בור (step 13) and אש (step 14).
steps.raayaObject: That the Torah lowered the guarding requirement for שן.

steps.title: The source for רגל: 'and he sent it loose'
steps.stepSummary: For רגל, the פסוק says 'וְשִׁלַּח', so the owner is חייב only when he acted like he sent his animal out loose.
steps.simpleTranslation: For foot, it is written: 'and he sent it.' This means he is not חייב until he acts in a way that is like sending it loose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the fourth damager, רגל, from the same פסוק. The Torah lowered the guarding for רגל too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'וְשִׁלַּח' describes the owner actively sending his animal out. So he is חייב only if his carelessness is like that. If he guarded it in a basic way, he is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: Foot: damage an animal does by trampling as it walks
'And he sent it loose' (שמות 22:4)

phrases.english: Foot – as it is written: "and he sent it"
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק as before, שמות 22:4.

phrases.english: – he is not liable until he does something like "and he sent it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 15, now for רגל.
steps.raayaObject: That the Torah lowered the guarding requirement for רגל.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows which word means foot and which means tooth
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא proves from other פסוקים that 'וְשִׁלַּח' refers to רגל and 'וּבִעֵר' refers to שן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: 'And he sent' means the foot, as it says, 'who send out the foot of the ox and the donkey.' 'And it feeds' means the tooth, as it says, 'as one consumes the dung until it is gone.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up the last two steps. It proves that these two words really refer to רגל and שן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 15 and 16 assumed that 'וּבִעֵר' is שן and 'וְשִׁלַּח' is רגל. The ברייתא shows this from other פסוקים that use the same words: one connects 'sending' with feet, and the other connects 'בִּעֵר' with consuming.

keyTerms.meaning: And so it says: brings another פסוק that uses the same word
Consumes, wipes out: the same root as וּבִעֵר

phrases.english: And it was taught: "and he sent" – this is the foot,
and so it says:
"who send out the foot of the ox and the donkey."
"and it feeds" – this is the tooth,
and so it says:
"as one consumes the dung until it is all gone."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the readings used in steps 15 and 16.
steps.raayaObject: That 'וְשִׁלַּח' means רגל and 'וּבִעֵר' means שן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא citing ישעיהו 32:20 and מלכים א 14:10.

steps.title: Conclusion: without that level of carelessness, the owner is not liable
steps.stepSummary: The owner is חייב only because he acted like 'sending' or 'feeding.' If he did not act that way, he is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason he is חייב is that he acted like 'and he sent' and 'and it feeds.' But if he did not act that way, he is not חייב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the פסוקים. For שן and רגל, a lower level of guarding is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liability depends on the owner acting like he sent or fed his animal. So if he guarded it even in a weaker way, he is פטור. This backs up step 11: our משנה can follow רבי מאיר, because for שן and רגל the Torah itself lowered the guarding requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is: points to what the ruling depends on
But if he did not do so, then no (he is not liable)

steps.whatToRemember: The Torah lowered the guarding for four damagers. בור: 'he did not cover it.' אש: 'the one who kindled.' שן: 'and it feeds.' רגל: 'and he sent it.' For these, basic guarding makes the owner פטור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the answer from step 11. Our משנה, which says a weaker guarding is enough for שן and רגל, does not have to follow only רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: The reason is that he did something like "and he sent" and "and it feeds,"
but if he did not do so – he is not liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical inference from the derivations in steps 15 to 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For שן and רגל, the owner is חייב only when his carelessness is like sending or feeding his animal. Otherwise, a weaker guarding is enough and he is פטור. This supports reading our משנה even according to רבי מאיר.

steps.title: רבה proves something from the word 'sheep' in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבה says the wording of the משנה supports the answer from step 11, that our משנה can follow רבי מאיר. The משנה says צאן instead of שור, which suggests it is talking only about the damages sheep usually do (שן and רגל), where the Torah reduced the guarding.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: The wording of the משנה also shows this, because it says 'sheep.' All this time we have been dealing with an ox, so let it say 'ox'! Why does it say 'sheep'? Is it not because the Torah reduced the guarding needed for them?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה brings support from the exact wording of the משנה. He asks why the משנה suddenly switched from 'ox' to 'sheep.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the משניות have been talking about an ox. Sheep don't usually gore; they mostly damage by eating (שן) and trampling (רגל). So רבה suggests the משנה picked sheep on purpose, because the Torah lowered the guarding only for שן and רגל. That supports the answer in step 11 that our משנה can follow רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: It is exact. The wording itself proves a point.
Sheep (small flock animals)
Since, after all
What is different? Why the change?
The Torah reduced the guarding needed for them

phrases.english: Rabba said:
The Mishnah is also precise in its wording,
since it teaches 'sheep.'
After all, we have been dealing with an ox all along,
so let it teach 'ox'!
What is different, that it teaches 'sheep'?
Is it not because the Torah reduced the guarding needed for them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from the wording of the משנה for the discussion about reduced guarding.
steps.raayaObject: That our משנה can follow רבי מאיר, because the Torah lowered the guarding specifically for שן and רגל, the damages sheep typically do.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's choice of the word צאן instead of שור.

steps.title: No, 'sheep' was chosen to leave out goring
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבה's proof. The משנה said צאן so we would not think it includes קרן. The Torah's lighter guarding is written only about שן and רגל, which are מועדין. The גמרא accepts this reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is because here, goring is not written about it; only eating and trampling are written about it. And it teaches us that eating and trampling are 'forewarned.' Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבה. It gives a different reason why the משנה said 'sheep,' and then accepts this new reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה had said 'ox,' we might have thought it also covers goring (קרן). Saying 'sheep' points only to שן and רגל, which are מועדין from the start. So the משנה could still follow רבי יהודה: it is teaching that his rule for a מועד (weaker guarding is enough) applies to שן and רגל. The wording does not prove that the משנה follows רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Goring, damage from an animal's horn
Eating and trampling damages
Forewarned: an animal expected to do this, so the owner is fully responsible
Learn from this; the point is accepted

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up. The גמרא is not saying sheep can never gore. It says the משנה chose 'sheep' as an example that points to שן and רגל and leaves out קרן.

phrases.english: No;

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְכָאן קֶרֶן לָא כְּתִיבָא בַּהּ,
phrases.english: it is because here, goring is not written about it,
phrases.notes: He means the Torah never wrote the lighter guarding rule about goring.

phrases.english: it is eating and trampling that are written about it;
and it teaches us
that eating and trampling are the ones that are forewarned.
Learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו; מִשּׁוּם דְכָאן קֶרֶן לָא כְּתִיבָא בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבה's proof by giving another reason for the word צאן.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the wording, not the law itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word צאן can be explained as excluding קרן, so it does not have to mean what רבה said.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה says 'sheep' to point to שן and רגל, the damages that are מועדין. So the משנה can still follow רבי יהודה, and the wording does not prove that it follows רבי מאיר.

steps.title: Four cases: exempt in human court, liable in Heaven's court
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהושע: four kinds of actions are פטור מדיני אדם but חייב בדיני שמים. They are breaking a fence in front of a friend's animal, bending a friend's grain toward a fire, hiring false witnesses, and holding back testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהושע said: There are four things where the one who does them is exempt by human law but liable by the laws of Heaven. They are: one who breaks down a fence in front of his friend's animal; one who bends his friend's standing grain in front of a fire; one who hires false witnesses to testify; and one who knows testimony for his friend and does not testify for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It brings a ברייתא that lists four cases where the court cannot make you pay, but Heaven still holds you responsible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In all four cases the person causes a loss, but only in an indirect way, so a human court does not make him pay. Still, he is morally guilty, and he should make it right to be cleared בדיני שמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt by human court
Liable by the laws of Heaven
One who breaks down a fence
Standing grain still in the field
False witnesses

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא sets up a key idea in נזיקין. Some damages are too indirect for a court to collect, yet the person is still responsible in Heaven's eyes.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehoshua said:
Four things, the one who does them
is exempt by human law,
but liable by the laws of Heaven.
And these are they:
one who breaks down a fence in front of his friend's animal,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַכּוֹפֵף קָמָתוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ בִּפְנֵי הַדְּלֵיקָה,
phrases.english: and one who bends his friend's standing grain in front of a fire,
and one who hires false witnesses to testify,
and one who knows testimony for his friend
and does not testify for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, connected to the subject of damage by animals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four cases are פטור מדיני אדם but חייב בדיני שמים.

steps.title: What case is 'breaking a fence' talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the first case in the ברייתא and asks what exact situation it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'One who breaks down a fence in front of his friend's animal.' What is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the ברייתא one case at a time. Here it asks for the exact situation of the first case, which sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breaking someone's fence sounds like direct damage, which a court should make you pay for. So the גמרא needs to explain what kind of fence this is, so that it fits 'exempt in human court.'

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the exact facts?

phrases.english: The Master said:
'One who breaks down a fence in front of his friend's animal.'
What is the case?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: הַפּוֹרֵץ גָּדֵר בִּפְנֵי בֶּהֱמַת חֲבֵירוֹ. הֵיכִי דָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining the first case of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact situation of breaking a fence in front of a friend's animal.

steps.title: It can't mean a strong wall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the case is a healthy, strong wall, but rejects it: breaking that would make him חייב even in a human court. It starts a new answer with 'אלא.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is a healthy, strong wall, then he should be liable by human law too! Rather...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests one possible case and throws it out. Then it starts giving a new answer, which continues past this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knocking down a sound wall is direct damage to the friend's property, so a court would make him pay. That clashes with the ברייתא's 'exempt by human law.' So the case must be something else, and the word 'אלא' begins that new answer.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say; brings a suggestion that is about to be rejected
A healthy, sound wall
Rather; brings in a new answer

phrases.english: If you say it is about a healthy, strong wall,
then he should be liable by human law too!
Rather,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests a possible answer to the question and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the ברייתא means a strong wall.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Breaking a strong wall is direct damage, which a human court would make him pay for. That contradicts 'exempt by human law.'
